EXPERT SESSION ON CYBER SECURITY & WOMAN SECURITY
Expert Talk on Cyber Security & Woman Sa
Expert Talk on Cyber Security & Woman Sa

Cybercrimes can be defined as "Offences that are committed against individuals or groups of individuals with a criminal motive to intentionally harm the reputation of the victim or cause physical or mental harm, or loss, to the victim directly or indirectly, using modern telecommunication networks such as Internet (networks including but not limited to Chat rooms, emails, notice boards and groups) and mobile phones (

Cybercrime may threaten a person or a nation’s security and financial health. Issues surrounding these types of crimes have become high-profile, particularly those surrounding hacking, copyright infringement, unwarranted mass-surveillance, sextortion, child pornography and child grooming. There are also problems of privacy when confidential information is intercepted or disclosed, lawfully or otherwise.

From the perspective of gender, 'cybercrime against women' is described as "Crimes targeted against women with a motive to intentionally harm the victim psychologically and physically, using modern telecommunication networks such as internet and mobile phones".

Cyber-crime and privacy breach in India has been growing exponentially every few months. According to the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), 1.71 lakh cybercrimes have been reported during 2014 -2017. The lack of user awareness about Internet, cyber laws and risks pose a big challenge in India.

In this scenario, it is important for every user to understand the risks associated with transactions in cyber space; implications of data leaks and privacy breaches through social media or email transactions and its remedies, are very important and should be taken care of with utmost priority. The session will enlighten the audience about cybercrime consequences with examples. When we consider the wide strata of users, from tech-savvy to new users, as well as different socio-economic conditions, demographics, culture and age, making users aware about the risk and saving them from cyber frauds is a challenge before law enforcement agencies as well as the government. All those who use the internet through cell-phones or PCs should be aware of the same.
To be well-versed with the term “Cyber Security & Women Safety” the session includes;
Types of Cyber Crime in Indian Scenario
Laws Related to Women & Its Implementation
Domestic Violence & Issue Relating to working Women

SSIP 2.0 aims to promote innovation and startups across traditional and new-age technologies and sunrise sectors. Innovations in clean and green energy, and efforts to address climate change, towards achieving India's pledge of net-zero emissions by 2070 will be encouraged. Thrust areas such as semiconductors, robotics, electric vehicles, waste management, artificial intelligence, machine learning, the Internet of Things, and Blockchain will also be in focus. However, the Policy aims to support sector-agnostic innovations and Startups.

A very informative and insightful webinar was organized by Computer Science and Engineering on Geographic Information Systems on 24th Oct, 20. It was with a collaboration with Orena Solutions. Speakers of the webinar were Mr. Saurin Mehta ( Results -driven operations Head & have 30+ years of experience in the filed of CAD/GIS/IT) and Ms. Sohini Munshi ( GIS Assistant Manager, S&P Global and have 9+ years of experience in Geo-informatics).

Orena Solutions is a visionary ICT company, headquartered in Vadodara, Gujarat, looking to rejuvenate the employability levels of the Indian workforce. With a collaboration with Orena Solutions we invited speakers for this webinar.

Webinar was started with a warm welcome. Mr. Saurin Mehta had given very briefed idea about the GIS. He discussed in very simple way that GIS allows us to view, understand, question, interpret, and visualize data in many ways that reveal relationships, patterns, and trends in the form of maps, globes, reports, and charts. He also introduced that A GIS helps you answer questions and solve problems by looking at your data in a way that is quickly understood and easily shared. GIS technology can be integrated into any enterprise information system framework.

Mr. Saurin Mehta gave brief ideas to the students regarding technical skills required for GIS like Mapping and Cartography, Geographical model of Earth, Deep understanding of drawing scales and Remote Sensing Software and Techniques. He also guided students regarding various tools and technologies required to be in the filed of GIS and Geo Informatics. Mr. Saurin Mehta had discussed various applications and usages of GIS in different areas.

After giving overview in various areas, Mr. Saurin Mehta had given detailed idea about How GIS can be applied to Water Network Management and its various layers. Mr. Mehta had also discussed about the modules of GIS in water management like water supply maintenance, Asset management, Consumer Management, Billing system, Employee management, Water quality management and Sewage management.

Mr. Mehta gave an overview of working of map location in GIS. He discussed that Map locations are used to find a feature and a finding patterns , Map Assets for distribution line information and Sewer Pipe Information. Mr. Mehta also gave a brief idea about map technical information and map densities. At the end sir had discussed a case study of Gas Distribution with project title of Re-Validation survey of Jagdishpur Haldia Pipeline. Sir had also discussed about career opportunities with multiple skill set and different profession were students can work.

After Mr. Mehta, Ms. Sohini Munshi had continued the session. She told that Python programming is a best programming language to build GIS based application. tableau software is also useful for GIS based applications. She has also gave overview of various professions were GIS can be used. For example in forest if we want to count total number of trees then through GIS we can do that.using various GIS techniques. Another example that she had discussed that through satellite images remotely we can plan where we can do the pipe lining. No need to reach at that place physically. GIS is also used in transportation and can be used in auto mated care driving system which map all the roads and hurdles with live data. Even virtual tour is also possible through GIS which is also initiated by national geographic. She also guided students regarding various tools and technologies used for develop GIS based application. She had introduced tableau , python , SQL, NoSQL, PostgreSQL as a basic building block to explore more about GIS.

In the last phase of the webinar, plenty queries were there in the student’s mind. Both speaker had solved their queries and gave proper guidance. Lastly, they threw some lights on ArcGIS , QGIS, Saga GIS tools to read and manipulate shape files. Ms. Abhilasha Vyas had asked few queries to read shape files in Saga GIS & Nature Earth data set. They suggested that the students who have good knowledge in python can develop their carrier in the field of GIS. At the end of this webinar, speakers gave brief overview of QGIS tool and how to view shape files and how to import shape files. Based on the shape file how we can see all the details about each dots in a shape file. The data which is incorporated with shape file could be manipulated and retrieved with the help of SQL queries.
This informative webinar was concluded with the hope to have such more collaborations and a training workshop to have a hand-son experience in the field of GIS.
Feedback of students were very satisfactory and also asked GSFCU management to arrange this kind of informative sessions with hands-on training's.

The series which aims at connecting and bonding the juniors with seniors, all the while not compromising their education.

The webinar commenced at 2:00 pm on 21st of November for the following 40 mins, on the online platform offered by Google Meet with approximately 70 enthusiastic attendees. Speaker Dhruvit mistry briefed us with the application of computers in various sectors of our life - Service sectors, Medical science, Education, Communication, Entertainment, Engineering department etc. Mr. Piyush, further shed light upon the backbone of computers- coding; and explained importance of coding in every sector. He also guided the keen participants about the right steps and sequence to start with coding and the computer languages. Role of coding in the era of computers is indispensable.

We all know about the ease at which we are living in this 21st century with computers and machines all around, rather the “smart machines”, that take away 70% of our work load. We ought to know about these and hence this webinar was an excellent medium to gain knowledge about the same. We are grateful that the speakers were ardent enough to interact with the participants and make this webinar worth it.

CITY CLEANLINESS DRIVE WITH VMC | GSFC University
GSFC University and Vadodara Municipal Corporation jointly organized Swachhhta Abhiyan at Vadodara.
GSFC University, in association to Vadodara Municipal Corporation undertook cleanliness drive at eight (8) locations in the jurisdiction of Vadodara Municipal Corporation on 02.03.2019 (Saturday).

At each locations, a team of students, faculties and non-teaching staff of GSFC university with the support of VMC team actively and sincerely participated. They cleaned the garbage, arranged for its disposal, distributed pamphlets about maintaining cleanliness, educated citizens of Vadodara to maintain cleanliness and undertook the survey about the cleanliness aspects. GSFC University President Shri P K Taneja, ( IAS Retd.) ,Shri Ajay Bhadoo, IAS ,Municipal Commissioner, Shri P J Aundhiya, GAS,  Dy. Municipal Commissioner(Health) with other officials of GSFCU and VMC also participated in the said cleanliness Drive.

In support to this drive, Shri P K Taneja, ( IAS Retd.),  President-GSFC University expressed that the objective of involving students in such drives is to increase their awareness about the social issues particularly the dignity of labour and to make them socially responsible . Shri Ajay Bhadoo, IAS, Municipal Commissioner-Vadodara expressed that cleanliness drive is a demand of time and to make it successful is a responsibility of one and all. Both the dignitaries took round of different locations of drive and motivated all participants. Shri P J Aundhiya, GAS , and his team extended whole hearted support to campaign.

HEALTH AND WELLNESS PROGRAMME AT GSFC UNIVERSITY

Health and fitness is the key to a long, active and enjoyable life. It is correctly stated that Health is the actual Wealth that a person can retain. Today's youth and Students need to realize the importance of staying healthy and fit. Also, being the future generation, they can play a vital role in creating awareness and maintaining a stable health regime in our society. Being healthy and fit in simple terms means taking good care of the body. We should remember that a healthy mind resides only in a healthy body. Good health of both mind and body helps one maintain the required energy level to achieve success in life.

A healthy and fit person is capable of living the life to the fullest, without any major medical or physical issues. Being healthy is not only related to the physical well-being of a person, it also involves the mental stability or the internal peace of a person.

All of us must strive to achieve wholesome health. Protecting your body from the intake of harmful substances, doing regular exercises, having proper food and sleep are some of the important instances that define a healthy lifestyle. Being fit allows us to perform our activities without being lethargic, restless or tired.

Generally, a healthy diet consists of taking a proper and healthy food which includes eating green and fresh vegetables, fruits, having milk, eggs, minerals, proteins and vitamins essential for a human’s lifestyle. Practicing Yoga including regular exercises in your daily routine also help you maintain your desired fitness, blood sugar and immunity level.
Good health not only means a state of absence of diseases in the body but a complete physical, mental, social as well as spiritual well-being of an individual.

With the above information keeping in mind GSFC University and Aarogyam club of the university students had organized in-campus a health and wellness programme for the University students and fraternity members from 3rd to 6th October 2018 at Vigyan Bhawan, School of Science with the help of Zydus Hospital, Anand. The program was inaugurated by Provost of the University.

Zydus Hospitals, Anand medical team had conducted basic medical tests for participants well-being including BMI, Eye check-up, Blood sugar, cardiac health and nutritional chart followed by physician consultation.

The program was meticulously organized and to avoid long queue and overcrowding at the program site. All stream students and staff members had been allocated specific time slot to minimal loss of their teaching hours and other activities respectively.

Total number of 883 participants has been screened in the four days long camp. It has been observed most of the students have been suffering from weak eye sights, poor diet in-take, junk food habits, and lack of exercises, stress and anxiety issues whereas hypertension, cardiac and blood pressure ailments have been identified in staff members respectively.

Corrosion Control Programme at GSFC University

Executive Development Centre at GSFC-U has successfully organized a 5-Days training program on “Corrosion Control” from August 27 to 31, 2018 for the industry professionals working in the operation, inspection and maintenance department who are dealing with the corrosion related issues at their plant.

The course equipped participants with skills critical for the evaluation of real-time Corrosion-related issues and for specifying predictive/preventive maintenance related to corrosion. This will help the organisations to reduce potential operational failures/damages leading to the forced shutdown, improve the overall availability of plant, and to devise the method to keep track of corrosion-related parameters during monitoring and inspection of equipment.

Total of 56 Executives from various industries participated in the programme. Some of the participating industries were: IOCL, OPaL, BASF, GACL, GNFC, GSFC, Transpek-Silox, GHCL, Deepak Nitrite, GSFC, Gujarat Gas Limited etc.

In the land where leaders like Gandhi and Ambedkar relentlessly strive for the abolition of the caste system, still some instances of caste and religious discrimination are reported in educational institutions. This sorry state of affairs is highly condemned by the UGC and Indian Law. Being temples of learning, educational institutions should inculcate in the minds of faculty and students that people should protect and defend the dignity of each individual through respect for human rights and the rule of law. With a view to providing a safe and secure learning ambiance for the students, GSFC University takes every possible step to eradicate any form of caste - based prejudices and discrimination in its facilities. Within GSFCU we value learning, mutual respect, teamwork, and diverse points of view. We relentlessly work for the harmony and co-existence amongst all.

GSFCU has set motivated goals for accomplishing measurable outcomes as to make a difference in our students & lives. The University has left no stone unturned to set an environment of freedom to the students during their stay here in the campus. In case there is a situation where in the student / faculty feels let down or humiliated due to some callous comment of someone or if he / she feels that they are being targeted by a particular faculty / peers due to their extremist and biased belief in caste, the person can lodge a complaint in the prescribed form that will reach a senior University official, which will be followed by an inquiry for justice to be delivered.
